claim: A wall record has one x_repeat and one y_repeat, and they scale its masked middle and its step bands alike. Glass hung on a wall whose sides stand at different heights forces the facade band above and below it to the glass's scale.
evidence: NBlood/source/build/src/engine.cpp:4425 and :4434 (setup_globals_wall2: the band's scale is taken from wal->yrepeat), called with the wall's own record for the upper band (:4721), the lower band even when cstat 2 borrows the next wall's picture (:4835), a one-sided wall (:4941) and the masked middle (:7232, renderDrawMaskedWall)

the owner, 2026-11-17: 'the glass should sit in a aperure/frame so glass texture scaling won't be colliding with facade texture' (projects/blood-city/experiments/shopfronts-streets/README.md:11; projects/blood-city/level/glass.py:22-24)
use: Hang a pane, a grille or bars only on a wall between two sectors of the same floor and ceiling (a reveal and a sash pocket behind the facade line); the facade's record keeps the facade's scale.

checked.how: engine.cpp setup_globals_wall2 (4398): globalyscale from wal->yrepeat at 4425 and 4434 (cited 4426, 4435). Its callers pass the wall's own record: 4721 (upper band), 4835 (lower band: setup_globals_wall1 takes the picnum of nextwall when cstat 2, but setup_globals_wall2(wal) keeps this wall's yrepeat), 4941 (one-sided), 7232 (renderDrawMaskedWall).
